why: All three checks confirm the divergence. (1) VERBATIM: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview.md line 227 contains the quoted sentence exactly. The whole line is a two-sentence-plus footnote whose earlier half describes `disable-model-invocation: true` in frontmatter; the second half is the quoted sentence and does not reverse it. The linked target (skills.md:635-663) specifies the shape: `skillOverrides` is a record of skill name -> one of `on` / `name-only` / `user-invocable-only` / `off`, absent means `on`, written by `/skills` into `.claude/settings.local.json`, and since v2.1.199 `off` also hides the skill from Remote Control and Agent SDK command lists. Plugin skills are explicitly EXEMPT (`Manage those through /plugin instead`). (2) CITED STATE: the file-authored half is confirmed present -- `packages/shared/src/capabilities/types.ts:129` documents and declares `skillDisableModelInvocation`, parsed at `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:296-298`, carried through `resolver.ts:1007-1009,1659-1661` and `views.ts:190-192`, and ENFORCED twice: `agent/core/prompt-builder.ts:405` filters the skill out of `<available_skills>` and `agent/base-agent.ts:2141` refuses a model-origin invocation of the same skill. The settings half has no Nessy reader. Note the claim's grep evidence line is incomplete: `grep -rail skilloverride` also hits `packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js`, `apps/electron/dist/resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js`, `apps/electron/resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js`, `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/{sdk.d.ts,sdk.mjs}` and several more docs/data files -- but every one of those is vendored Claude Agent SDK settings-schema text inside a build artifact, not a Nessy implementation. Zero hits under any `src/` tree (`grep -rn -a -i skilloverride packages/*/src apps/*/src` is empty). (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier, one layer up and one down. UP -- every settings-side skill control we do have was checked and none reproduces the behaviour: `disableBundledSkills` (`config/bundled-skills-settings.ts`, `config/storage.ts:1337-1353`) is a bulk on/off for bundled skills, not per-skill and not a visibility ladder; the native-source `enabled` flag (`native-sources.ts:551,594` -> `resolver.ts:1595` `record.sourceEnabled !== false`) is set only on `kind === 'source'` records (MCP/api/local), never on `kind === 'skill'` records built by `skillRecords()` at `native-sources.ts:266-290`, so it cannot disable a skill; session selection (`resolver.ts:737-739`, fed at `server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:859`) supplies `enabledSourceKeys` for `kind === 'source'` only and no production producer supplies `transientlyDisabledKeys`. DOWN -- `disableModelInvocation` reaches the runtime exclusively from SKILL.md frontmatter or a plugin skill declaration; nothing merges a settings layer into it. SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM CHECK (the `disallowed-tools` trap): the per-capability toggle `setCapabilityEnabled(pluginKey, capabilityId, enabled)` (`plugins/management-service-v2.ts:283`, `plugins/store.ts:266`, RPC `server-core/src/handlers/rpc/plugins.ts:94`, UI `PluginInfoPage.tsx:334-343`) is keyed by `pluginKey` and therefore covers PLUGIN skills only -- which is precisely the population Claude's own page exempts from `skillOverrides`. It is the `/plugin` equivalent, not the `skillOverrides` equivalent, so it does not refute the row. NATIVE skills (`skillRecords` over home `~/.claude|.nessy/skills`, the managed config dir, the workspace `skills/` dir, and project `.nessy-agent`/`.claude` skills dirs) have no enable/disable/visibility control in any settings layer or UI. VENDORED-SDK CAVEAT, checked and rejected as a refutation: `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:4635` types `skillOverrides`, and `claude-agent.ts:305` passes `settingSources: ['user','project','local']`, so the SDK does read the settings files that could carry the key -- but `claude-agent.ts:1118` puts `Skill` in `disallowedTools`, skills reach the model through Nessy's own capability/prompt-builder path instead, and the Claude provider is off by default (`NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE`). No Nessy-owned code path honours the key on any backend. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` section 3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) -- none touches skill visibility. NOT a de-brand or dropped-subscription-flow difference: skill visibility is provider-neutral and the fork ships a full native skills subsystem.
correctedState: Confirmed gap, with the scope narrowed and the evidence line corrected. No Nessy source reads `skillOverrides`; the only hits outside docs are vendored Claude Agent SDK settings-schema text inside build artifacts (`packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js`, `apps/electron/{dist/,}resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js`) and `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/{sdk.d.ts:4635,sdk.mjs}` -- not an implementation. The frontmatter half is not merely 'supported' but enforced on both halves: `prompt-builder.ts:405` omits a `disable-model-invocation` skill from `<available_skills>` and `base-agent.ts:2141` refuses its model-origin invocation. The missing piece is specifically a settings layer for NATIVE skills: plugin skills already have the documented-equivalent control (`setCapabilityEnabled`, which is Claude's `/plugin` path and which `skillOverrides` explicitly exempts), while a skill under a workspace/home/project `skills/` directory -- the exact 'checked into a shared project repo' case the docs name -- can only be hidden or narrowed by editing its SKILL.md. Also missing is the four-state ladder itself: we have a binary (`disable-model-invocation` plus the separate `user-invocable`), not `on`/`name-only`/`user-invocable-only`/`off`, and no equivalent of `off` suppressing the skill from Agent SDK / Remote Control command lists. `disableBundledSkills` exists but is bulk and bundled-only.
